text:
alex: Quick post-upgrade alert. After upgrading Cilium to v1.17.1 on the eu-gpu nodepool at 02:40 UTC a subset of GPU nodes started showing sporadic pod-to-pod packet loss and RDMA connections tearing down. A couple of long-running training jobs crashed with 'rdma: connection reset' errors.
oncall-bot: ALERT: net-loss spike detected on nodepool eu-gpu-2 (metric: pod_packet_loss) at 2026-03-17T02:55:11Z.
maria: confirmed on prod-west too. Noticing `cilium_vxlan` device present even though we previously used `kube-router` direct routing for IB servers.
sam: can someone paste `cilium status --verbose` and the output of `ip -d link` from an affected host? Also try pings with small (1400) and jumbo (9000) payloads between two GPU pods.
alex: logs from node eu-gpu-2-node07 below plus ping results.
``n
Mar 17 02:42:11 eu-gpu-2-node07 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:85:00.0: NIC Link is Up
Mar 17 02:43:03 eu-gpu-2-node07 cilium-agent[1012]: info: using tunnel mode: vxlan
Mar 17 02:43:04 eu-gpu-2-node07 cilium-agent[1012]: warning: auto-detected mtu 1450 != device mtu 9000
Mar 17 02:43:05 eu-gpu-2-node07 kernel: rdma_cm: <peer> - event RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED
Mar 17 02:43:07 eu-gpu-2-node07 kernel: NETDEV WATCHDOG: cilium_vxlan (mlx5_core): transmit queue 0 timed out
```

# ping from pod gpu-train-1 -> gpu-train-2
ping -c 6 -s 1400 10.40.3.12
64 bytes from 10.40.3.12: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=0.29 ms
--- 2% packet loss ---

ping -c 6 -s 9000 10.40.3.12
--- 50% packet loss ---

jia: this looks like the new default tunnel/encapsulation in 1.17 is creating a VXLAN interface with a ~1450 MTU, which fragments RDMA/jumbo frames. On our 100Gb IB-equipped hosts we rely on jumbo MTU for direct RDMA. If Cilium switched us to VXLAN with a lower MTU, RDMA will break.
sam: on host, `ip -d link` shows: `eth0 mtu 9000 state UP`, `cilium_vxlan mtu 1450`, `kube-bridge mtu 1450`. So tunnel device indeed lowered path MTU.
maria: did helm values change? Check the cilium ConfigMap/Helm values for `tunnel:` and `auto-mtu:`. We previously had `tunnel: disabled` on gpu nodepools.
alex: helm history indicates chart v1.17.1 set `tunnel: vxlan` by default and `auto-mtu: true`. Previous release explicitly disabled tunnel.

sam: mitigation brainstorm:
- rollback Cilium to prior stable chart on gpu nodepools (fast, local change)
- flip `tunnel: disabled` in Cilium config and add host routes / BGP for pod CIDRs (more intrusive)
- bump VXLAN MTU if fabric allows (likely constrained by cloud subnet limits)
- cordon/evacuate affected nodes and patch agents with a node-level MTU override

jia: immediate plan: target a limited rollback on the eu-gpu nodepool only to avoid disruption elsewhere. We should also create a preflight test that runs a jumbo-ping and a basic RDMA handshake on any nodepool with IB before upgrading.
sam: agreed. I'm starting a rollback to cilium 1.16.11 on eu-gpu-2 now (reuse values, only change chart version). I'll watch `kubectl -n kube-system rollout status ds/cilium` and network metrics.

srebot: RUNBOOK: network/cilium-mtu-regression (section 2: rollback flow).
maria: I'm checkpointing affected training jobs and draining the worst nodes so we can reduce job restarts. Filing INFRA ticket: internal/INFRA-1137.

[~25 minutes later]
sam: rollback complete on eu-gpu-2 nodepool. `cilium status` shows bpf programs loaded and host routing active. Pod-to-pod ping with 9000-byte payloads now shows 0% loss and RDMA reconnections succeed for two restarted jobs.
alex: excellent. Next steps: add a pre-upgrade verification job into our upgrade pipeline: 1) ping -s 9000 between pods, 2) run small RDMA connect test, 3) verify `ip -d link` MTU alignment. If any fail, abort the upgrade. Also open upstream issue with Cilium (attach logs + ebpf attach errors) to see if eBPF helper changes are affecting mlx5 offload.
jia: I'll open the PR to default `tunnel: disabled` for nodepools labeled `redwood/ib=true` and add the preflight checks to the cluster-upgrade playbook.
maria: closing alerts and updating incident notes. :white_check_mark:
